posts.cooked:
well, on timelines/realities. Look at it this way.

 

There was Sentinels of the -Multiverse- - The Multiverse was open, active, possible to move between timelines/realities (As per Shattered Timelines, Ivana Romanof, XTREME Prime Wardens, O-X, Be The Gate, Ect, ect... ect...). We have a central timeline/reality (that of all the heroes and villains of the card game) but there is a lot of crossing over back and forth between timelines/realities. Lots of weird things around that, so its very muddy as to what is the 'real' timeline/reality. In fact, in essence the overall story of The Multiverse is that ALL of the timelines/realities are real, all of them can be crossed over into by various abilities, powers, spells, and all of them have an impact on the cruical point (a 'Fixed Point, perhaps?) of OblivAeon assaulting.

This multiple timelines/realities P'O'd OblivAeon, who idenitified the crux of the multiverse at Earth. He starts collapsing timelines in an attempt to destroy the Multiverse.

 

After the fight, the timelines/realities are cut off from each other. We know of 2 that stabilize and remain.

 

1) - The end result is that Rook City is only damaged, and things go on (The RPG)

2) - The end result is that Rook City is destroyed, and its a bad place (Tactics)

 

There is nothing to say that either of these timelines has its origins in the exact same 'Centralized' timeline as Sentinels of the Multiverse. It is entirely possible that the Tactics timeline/reality grew from a point where Kismet did not become a villain or have powers, beyond a simple curse of Setback (or even Setback's origin is slightly different, we don't know - for instance, his good/bad luck is a natural power, not a curse) It is simply one of the stabilized timelines that is cut off from the others that we know of, and that we pick up from some time after the OblivAeon event, where Rook City has been majorly destroyed. 

 

Nothing at all states that it is the exact same up to the point of OblivAeon as the 'centralized' timeline of SotM. Only that it is one of the timelines we can follow story wise after OblivAeon. Given how muddy the timeline/reality cross over is in SotM, this is entirely possible that a side timeline, without Kismet being a villain goes along just fine until the OblivAeon event (where ALL realities and timelines cross into one fixed point) and then goes its own way afterwards. Perhaps being affected (by gaining Setback, if he didn't exist as a hero before) or perhaps just having its own reasons for things (ie, Setback got his luck powers a different way)

 

3 different timelines/realities, for instance all come together at the OblivAeon event. ALL timelines/realities come together at the OblivAeon Event. Thats kinda his point, he's collapsing them all together to destroy them.

|   |   |
\    |  /
  \  | /
 OBLIVAEON
  /  |  \
 /   |   \ 
|    |   |

 

and that in turn means that one of those side timelines/realities could have been Tactics before OblivAeon, meaning that its entirely possible Kismet never existed in the Tactics timeline/reality

posts.name: lynkfox
posts.cooked:
Alternatively, there is another possible reason.

 

Something Kismet does during the OblivAeon Event helps cause the Rook City destroyed, Sentinel Tactics timeline/reality and that same thing also erases her from that timeline/reality. So that it goes on, but she never existed in it.

posts.name: lynkfox
posts.cooked:
(sorry, tripple post cause of editing bug shenanigans)

 

And that something that she does, the universe automatically rights itself after, so that in that timeline things continue the same just no Kismet, not meaning that the 'Centralized, Proper Canonical' SotM timeline/reality is different, just that she did something to erase herself from the Tactics timeline/reality. 

 

Truthfully, i find my first reasoning to be easier to except, though story wise I could totally see Kismet having her 'Moment of Heroic Glory' that erases her from the resulting timeline/reality

posts.name: dprcooke
posts.cooked:
@Lynkfox - What threw me for a loop was that I had always assumed that the Tactics/RPG timelines had both branched off of the same orginal timeline (the "primary reality" as Adam calls it).   As a result, both timelines would have shared the same pre-OblivAeon "past", having diverged at some point near/during OblivAeon.  While true (as far as I know) that Christopher/Adam have never expressly stated this to be the case, the format of the podcast definitely suggests it: We cover the history of the primary reality leading up to OblivAeon, followed by the OblivAeon event itself, and then discuss what the two distinct future timelines are.

If, as it now appears, the two realities do not share a common past, I have so many questions!  If Kismet does not exist in the RPG timeline, what other differences are there?  How many other villains (or heroes) simply don't exist?  Are there new ones?  As has already been asked, if it's the case that Gabrielle Adhin exists but doesn't have powers, how did Pete get his luck powers in the RPG timeline?

On that last question, I'd like to advance one more theory: When Gabrielle cursed Pete, some strange interraction occured between her powers (and the specifically great power behind the curse) and OblivAeon that resulted in Gabrielle cursing Pete not just in one timeline, but in multiple (possibly even all) timelines.  Since her powers already deal with threads of reality and OblivAeon allows timelines to merge and people to cross between them, I don't think it's too huge of a leap to believe that she could have somehow cursed every Pete.  Or perhaps it was somehow caused by "reality bouncing back" as Christopher and Adam describe in the episode?

I think i view it more as Pre OblivAeon all the timeline/realities are fluid. They cross over, a lot (at fixed points like Vanessa and the oblivAeon event for every timeline/reality, as well as other times in just a choatic random fashion for random timeline/realities) - Pre OblivAeon, a timeline/reality where Kismet does not become a villain is part of the 'Main' timeline/reality bundle that makes up all of Sentinels of the Multiverse. Sure, there is a Primary Timeline/Reality - that being the one the readers view point originates from, but all of the others are still part of the same whole - ie, the Multiverse. Remember, after OblivAeon there is no more Multiverse. They don't mean that as just there is no more card game, but that travel between timelines/realities is impossible. There is no more overlapping, fluidity.

The Multiverse as a whole contains both a timeline/reality where Kismet is a villain and one where she isnt.

 

Honestly, i feel like it is just leaving room for them to add and remove characters that are not from the card game into the other two as they wish without having to explain where they where during the card game
